## Fictional social budget – no current entitlement claims
M1Pension benefits120million, contributions90, gap30. A adds30contributions; B tax grant30within unchanged100public budget; C cuts benefits30. New funded saving20yearly while old pay-as-you-go benefits still cost120; return/inflation uncertain. Health choices higher contributions or copayments with hardship protection address supplied rising medical costs.
M2Four equal households10,15,25,50; net10from highest to lowest yields20,15,25,40; re-sort. Lorenz/Gini=1−sum((Y_i+Y_(i−1))·0.25),cumulativeincomeY,Y0=0. Equal Gini does not ensure equal poverty.
M3Two100-person groupsL/H: primary100/400,taxes20/100. L benefit40but50%take-up; actual recipients get40, not everyone20. Full take-up reform costs4,000instead of2,000, financed by an additional20taxperH. Free education20forL is not automatically cash and use/quality is uncertain. Separate means and individual situations.
M4Household equivalent monthly income1,050; median2,200, relative threshold60%. No public transport, car250, no training access. Compare100cash versus same-budget transport pass with a usable connection; displaced public spending remains open.
1.Assess pension A–C and health alternatives by finance/incentives/access/distribution/risks, justifying a conditional choice.
2.Draw/label both Lorenz curves and calculate/interpretGini without equating inequality/poverty.
3.Compare pay-as-you-go/new funding, needs/transition burden, demography/productivity/market risk and generations.
4.Calculate disposable group means before/after actual take-up/finance; assess heterogeneous recipients and noncash services with assumptions.
5.Diagnose poverty/access, compare measures/exclusions and propose a funded measurable mix beyond the income indicator.

4.Lbefore100−20+.5·40=100,H300;afterL120,H280. BeforeLindividuals80or120, not everybody100;afterall120. Additional cost2,000matchesH100·20. Education may help but is not automatic20cash or guaranteed immediate income; make assumptions/indicators explicit.
